LESSON: MARRIAGE AND FAMILY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 1.2: Marriage and Family

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Marriage and Family. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is marriage an important institution?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family
2. discuss the negative results of early marriage
3. identify values needed to avoid early marriage

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MARRIAGE AND FAMILY
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Marriage and Family helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: MARRIAGE AND FAMILY
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Marriage and Family” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Discuss the negative results of early marriage

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss the negative results of early marriage. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss the negative results of early marriage.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Marriage and Family.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss the negative results of early marriage. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Identify values needed to avoid early marriage

What this means
In this part you learn to identify values needed to avoid early marriage. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify values needed to avoid early marriage.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify values needed to avoid early marriage. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Marriage and Family is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Marriage and Family” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Marriage and Family. (skill: discuss the negative results of early marriage)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: identify values needed to avoid early marriage)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Marriage and Family to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family.
3. Practise this skill: discuss the negative results of early marriage.
4. Practise this skill: identify values needed to avoid early marriage.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Marriage and Family from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Marriage and Family: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Marriage and Family?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is marriage an important institution?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Marriage and Family means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family.
5. Be able to: discuss the negative results of early marriage.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
